articles.title: England v Sri Lanka: men’s tri-series cricket one-day international – live
articles.summary: Updates from Rawalpindi, play starts at 9am BST. Does cricket need a Ballon d’Or? | Mail Rob. 3rd over: England 5-0 (Banton 2, Duckett 3) Duckett survives a run-out chance after taking a quick single on the off side.
body: 12th over: England 60-0 (Banton 50, Duckett 9) Banton reverse-sweeps a single to bring up an excellent half-century from 48 balls. He’s hit nine fours, although the majority were timed rather than hit. It’s Banton’s fourth 50+ score in five innings since he was moved up to open.
11th over: England 57-0 (Banton 49, Duckett 7) Banton pulls Malinga for two to move within one run of another half-century. He has 49 from 46 balls, Duckett 7 from 20.

10th over: England 54-0 (Banton 47, Duckett 6) The left-arm spinner Dunith Wellalage, recalled today, comes on to bowl the last over of the Powerplay. Banton hoicks a reverse sweep over the top for four to bring up an uneven fifty partnership. He’s one hit away from his own fifty.
“One of the problems with a tri-series is that nobody turns up for the neutral games,” writes Andrew Goudie. “I hope there will be more of a crowd in the evening.”

articles.title: Leicester hit their lowest ebb - but is Martin turning things around?
articles.summary: Leicester are 10th in League One, 10 years after winning the Premier League. After hitting their lowest ebb, are there now grounds for optimism?
body: A decade ago, they were reigning 5,000-1 Premier League champions and the toast of the world.
Five years ago, the Foxes lifted the FA Cup for the first time and were challenging for Champions League qualification.
Since then they have fallen fast with financial problems, points deductions and the drop to the third tier, leaving the club up for sale.
But back-to-back wins this week - for the first time since last November - have shown the shoots of recovery after a stuttering start.

articles.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
articles.summary: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey. “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says.
body: Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.”

Ameobi’s “A” was often the family home, situated within a few pitch lengths of Newcastle’s St James’ Park, and “B” was frequently the club’s then Benwell base, where he would head for academy training.

“It built incredible resilience in me,” Ameobi says. “That really helped me in a sporting context in my career but also as a person, understanding that, irrespective of what people thought of me, what really mattered was the value I put on myself.”

That young boy running in fear became the scorer of 79 goals in 397 appearances for Newcastle including seven against their local rivals, Sunderland. The likelihood is that some of those he fled from while wearing a club tracksuit subsequently cheered him.
points: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey.

articles.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
articles.summary: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding. St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time. Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties. For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis.
body: From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.
Daniel Edelman scored the decisive penalty, with backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt making a save on Columbus’ first attempt, himself having entered the match in the second half.

Fittingly given their home city’s rich soccer history, City’s first trophy is also the nation’s oldest. Wednesday marked the 109th final in the history of the Open Cup, which was first held in 1913–14 and has run continuously save for a two-year hiatus during the Covid-19 pandemic.

However, St Louis did so with MLS’s youngest manager – Yoann Damet, the 36-year-old Frenchman who was previously Wilfried Nancy’s top assistant in Columbus but was passed over for the top job after Nancy left. St Louis will be thankful that he was.

articles.title: From Bury to AC Milan: Bournemouth's journey to 'dreamland'
articles.summary: Fifteen years to the day after they lost at home to Bury in League One, Bournemouth host seven-time champions of Europe AC Milan in the Europa League.
body: "It's not long ago we were playing Oldham Athletic and Hartlepool United in League One. Now I'm about to watch us play AC Milan.
It is a game between the club that refused to die against the 11-time European Cup finalists on what promises to be a momentous night in the history of the 127-year-old Dorset club.
"Over the last decade, my hometown club has achieved dreamland," Tony Pulis, who played for Bournemouth before managing them from 1992-94 and still lives in the area, tells BBC Sport.
"It's an unbelievable story, when I think back to what the club was like when I was player, coach and then manager there in the 1980s and early 1990s, but one that hopefully just keeps going."

articles.title: Who is close to a yellow card suspension in Champions League?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains what the rules are regarding yellow card suspensions in this season's Champions League
body: Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.
This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.
The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.
During the opening three rounds of Champions League, 16 players received two yellow cards, meaning they are now two cautions away from a one-match ban.

articles.title: Warriors face major Kristaps Porzingis setback as Stephen Curry speaks out
articles.summary: Stephen Curry has admitted the Golden State Warriors face a difficult situation after Kristaps Porzingis was reportedly sidelined indefinitely with a health issue that has left him considering retirement.
body: The Latvian centre was expected to play a key role for Golden State this season after signing a two-year, $40 million contract extension during the offseason.
However, recurring symptoms of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) have disrupted those plans, leaving the Warriors uncertain about when, or whether, he will return.
Speaking after Golden State’s 127-105 defeat to the Los Angeles Lakers, Curry acknowledged the impact Porzingis’ situation has had on both the player and the team.

“It’s a hard one for all reasons,” Curry said, as reported by ESPN’s Anthony Slater. “Personally, first and foremost. Then us as a team…We always said availability was a big factor for our team. It’s no secret that (center) spot was an important one for us, especially with the skillset.”

articles.title: Carra: Fernandes comments 'disgraceful', but Carrick's time may be up
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher has criticised Bruno Fernandes for questioning Man Utd's tactics following their 4-1 defeat to Como, but believes that it could be the end of the line for Michael Carrick.
body: Fernandes questioned the decision to not press Como man-to-man post-match, while Carrick responded in his press conference by saying "if you don't run back, you ain't going to win".

Fernandes' claims come just over a week after Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy following the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid. Carragher was critical of the Argentine's comments, and shared a similar stance when it came to the Manchester United captain's verdict.
"We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order for calling out the hierarchy," Carragher said on CBS Sports.

"For Bruno Fernandes to do that, it is a disgrace. Last season he was Player of the Year. That was due to Michael Carrick coming in as manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick. He put him back in his right position.

articles.title: Where is it going wrong for Carrick's Man Utd?
articles.summary: Thursday marks five months exactly since Man Utd announced Michael Carrick would be staying on as head coach. There will be little mood for celebrating anniversaries the morning after his worst night in the role.
body: The 4-1 thumping in Como left Carrick, in his own words, "angry". It also ruptured open divisions in the camp, with club captain Bruno Fernandes criticising the tactical plan.
United have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League season and that European humbling means they are now seven without a win across all competitions.
It's a shocking collapse in form from the brilliant run at the back end of last season which convinced United to sign Carrick up until 2028. So what's gone wrong?

This week, it was Fernandes. Last week, it was Lisandro Martinez hitting out at the hierarchy. The centre-back had technical director Jason Wilcox in his sights when he criticised the club for not strengthening the squad further in the summer transfer window.

articles.title: NFL Awards Ballot: Can Josh Allen Run His Way To MVP? Will Kenneth Walker Buck Trend?
articles.summary: Josh Allen is playing elite again, and Kenneth Walker is on track to break the rushing record. However, we have another player leading the MVP race.
body: The title used to belong to Lamar Jackson, but Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is clearly the best running quarterback in the league.

Allen leads all quarterbacks with 240 rushing yards and tops the NFL with eight touchdowns this season. Extrapolate that over 17 games and thatâs 680 rushing yards and 22 (!) rushing touchdowns. The former would be his most in a season since 2022, and the latter would be a career high.

Last year, Allen and the Bills made a concerted effort to not use him as a rusher as much. However, Allen still finished with 579 rushing yards and 14 rushing touchdowns before running for 99 yards and two scores in the two playoff games, including a four-turnover effort in a loss to the Denver Broncos.

New Buffalo head coach Joe Brady appears to have reignited Allen by unleashing him more as a runner. The obvious concern is Allen suffering a significant injury on scrambles. But as heâs aged, Allen has gotten better at protecting himself when he runs the football.
